headline: KSE-100 catches its breath at 177,623.88 (-0.36%) after Monday's 4.23% surge, while a Cabinet refining-policy nod and PTC's profit turnaround headline a busy news day.
summary: The index eased 638 points to 177,623.88 today, a normal pause after Monday's near-4% surge, not a reversal. Two material stories drove the tape: the Cabinet Committee on Energy approved Brownfield Refining Policy amendments (Euro-V fuel standard, Gulf investor roadshows) that lit up ATRL on roughly 3x normal volume, and PTC posted a Rs4.7bn 1HCY26 profit versus a Rs9.9bn loss a year ago, yet its stock fell anyway. Oil stays the swing factor: Brent is off 1.6% today but still up almost 19% on the month, which is why the desk's geo-risk gauge sits at a moderate 63/100, driven mostly by the still-unresolved Middle East conflict. Banks' results season and last week's S&P sovereign upgrade keep the broader backdrop constructive.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: H1 results season is running hot (UBL profit +33% YoY on record deposits) and last week's S&P sovereign upgrade to 'B' underpins the group; HBL and BAFL report over the next two weeks.

sectors.name: E&P / Oil & Gas
sectors.why: Brent is still roughly 19% higher than a month ago even after today's pullback, a direct tailwind for OGDC/PPL/MARI/POL per the desk's geo-risk sector read.

sectors.name: Refining
sectors.why: Today's Brownfield Refining Policy approval (Euro-V standard, Gulf roadshows) is a genuine tailwind for ATRL/NRL/PRL, but these are structurally thin-margin businesses -- cheap on paper, not yet a clean re-rating story.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Still on the macro desk's favoured list as a domestic-demand defensive; FFC and EFERT both report H1 results tomorrow (2026-07-29), a near-term read on the sector's health.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: The same oil strength that helps E&P squeezes OMC margins on the cost side, and a June current-account deficit adds circular-debt risk on fuel pass-through.

sectors.name: Cement, Autos & Textiles/exporters
sectors.why: Still on the macro desk's avoid list on rate, currency and energy-cost pressure; nothing in today's news changes that.

watchlist.angle: The desk's highest-confidence live signal today: an OBV volume-divergence trigger with a 96.6% historical hit rate (89 backtested trades, 83.3% out-of-sample hit rate) -- volume building ahead of price. Fundamentals back it up: rated 'attractive', cheap P/E around 6.5, a fat 32% net margin. H1 results due 2026-07-31.
watchlist.risk: Pays no dividend, so the whole return rides on a re-rating; it also sits outside core KSE-100 coverage with thinner liquidity, and the upcoming results could reset the setup either way.

watchlist.angle: Ground zero for today's refining story -- traded on roughly 3x normal volume, up nearly 3% on the day, RSI north of 67, directly on the back of the Cabinet's Brownfield Refining Policy approval. Cheap on paper (P/E around 4.7); H1 results land 2026-08-11.
watchlist.risk: It's a policy amendment, not an executed deal yet, and an RSI above 67 means a good chunk of the good news may already be in the price.

watchlist.angle: Same Brownfield Refining Policy tailwind as ATRL, even cheaper on paper (P/E under 4), with H1 results due the same day, 2026-08-11.
watchlist.risk: Thin net margin (around 2%) and no dividend -- a refiner whose profits swing hard with crack spreads and the rupee, so the policy boost has to show up in real numbers, not just sentiment.

watchlist.angle: The macro desk keeps E&P favoured while Brent sits roughly 19% above where it was a month ago; POL screens 'attractive' -- cheap P/E near 7, a covered dividend yield near 11%, and improving forward earnings. H1 results also due 2026-08-11.
watchlist.risk: This is a call on oil, not PSX-specific news -- Brent is already down over 1% today, and a sharper reversal removes the main tailwind fast.

catalysts.event: H1CY26 results due: FFC, EFERT, HCAR, AGL, JSML
H1CY26 results (BML, AKBL, COLG, CSAP, EPCL, KTML, SLGL) and last day to buy UBL for its confirmed dividend
PBS releases July CPI, the first print since the recent oil whipsaw
HBL H1CY26 results; NESTLE goes ex-dividend
H1CY26 results: ATRL, NRL, POL -- first hard numbers since today's refining-policy news

risks: The Middle East conflict is still live and is the single biggest driver of the desk's geo-risk score (conflict/escalation stress reads 100/100) -- Brent is still up almost 19% on the month despite today's dip, and a fresh escalation could undo today's calm fast.
The rupee keeps creeping weaker (USD/PKR +0.47% today, +0.22% on the month), and a disorderly move would force a hawkish SBP response and hit risk appetite market-wide.

The market didn't reward PTC's own turnaround story -- the stock closed lower on the day it reported a 1HCY26 profit versus a year-ago loss, and its trailing fundamentals still tag it lossmaking. A reminder that a good headline doesn't always show up in the same day's tape.
